To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immune system of a child is programmed in utero and in infancy by the mother and environment.

the immune system of a newborn infant is in a state of "immunological naivete" which is characterized by an inability to produce interferon-gamma and interleukin-12 in response to a variety of stimuli, and that the development of the Th1 subset of helper cells is dependent on the production of these cytokines.

1) the incidence of asthma in children is related to the prevalence of asthma and allergies in the community; 2) the incidence of childhood asthma and allergic diseases has increased dramatically in the past 30 years; 3) the incidence of atopy in children is related both to the prevalence of atopy and the prevalence of asthma in the community; and 4) the incidence of allergic diseases in adults is related to the incidence of allergic disease in children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of viruses in the development of allergic diseases and the possibility of using vaccines to prevent or treat these diseases.
the role of viruses in the inception of atopic diseases and the development of asthma.
the role of the T cell response in the control of mycobacterial infection, the mechanisms involved in the development of protective immunity and the factors which influence this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is insufficient to prove that viral infection of the respiratory tract is an essential cause of asthma or that it is a significant cause of asthma.
asthma and atopy are the result of a Th2-type response to a variety of environmental antigens and allergens.
there is no conclusive evidence that there is any link between viral infections and schizophrenia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Thl phenotype, as defined by the cytokine profile, the pattern of antibody production, and the pattern of disease susceptibility, is established early in life and is influenced by environmental factors such as infection.
the development of asthma and atopy is associated with the development of a Th2-type response, and that the factors responsible are likely to be those that determine the Thl/Thz balance.

the immune system of the infant is in a state of flux during the first 6 months, and the balance between Thl and Th2 responses may be determined by environmental factors, including the presence or absence of maternal antibodies.
